comment: Dr. Warrick is a very nice person but not a great professor. There is a lot of homework which feels more like busywork, and the assignments are repetitive. He goes much more in depth than any of the other intro bio courses I have heard about all while talking about how he's not going to go into specifics.

Dr. Warrick is a very kind professor, and I enjoyed his lectures. Overall the tests were pretty difficult, but manageable, and the amount of work assigned mostly included readings and a couple of outside assignments. His slides are pretty sparse, and so it is very important to take notes in class.

As a person, Dr. Warrick is great. As a professor, he assigns a ton of work, and his lectures aren't very helpful for the tests. He definitely isn't the worst option for Bio 200, but he isn't the best either. He gives a lot of partial credit on exams, but he has to because they're so long that there's barely time to finish.

Dr. Warrick is a really nice guy and a good professor. Lecture's aren't super helpful and his slides don't have much information on them so it's key to take notes during class. Lots of textbook reading and weekly reading quizzes that got increasingly difficult. Exams are tough but he gives lots of partial credit. His office hours are very helpful.

Dr. Warrick is overall a good professor. He is a little awkward but very nice. He is understanding and always willing to answer questions. His tests can be hard and he assigns A LOT of work, sometimes too much. You must take notes on the textbook because he gives weekly quizzes. If you do ALL the work and ask questions you will get a good grade.

Dr. Warrick is an easy grader who always give partial credits on exams. He's always accessible outside of class & want you to be successful; he will explain everything you don't understand in the way that makes sense to you. He also does what he can to improve your overall grade, final grade are not base on numbers but what he think you deserves.
My only complain was that the material covered on tests was a little ambiguous at times. Other then that he was really great; get ready to learn all about Drosophila.
Did not give help in or out of class. Does not know how to teach very well. Did not use his own powerpoints. Had no idea what was going on in lab.

All in all a solid professor. Expects that you give an honest effort, and will be fair if he sees that you are doing so. There is a lot of note-taking in this class, and you pretty much have to do it if you want to do well. Not an easy professor, but not painfully hard either. Grading is hard early in the course, but gets easier.
Very helpful and VERY smart. A little awkward at times, but once you get past that, he's great!

his bio 199 class was definetly the hardest out of all of them, but most useful,but what i leanred has been SO useful in my genetics class this semester ive barely had to study. he is a very smart, lectures are boring just because he feeds you so much information. tests usually cover about 1/3 of the material he teaches, but you have to know it all

He doesnt explain things well, doesnt give u sufficient help outside of class unless u have precise questions, complains a LOT!...doesnt return homework or tests for weeks (sometimes months) and gives u no help when it comes to tests..no study guides, reviews, etc...
Dr. Warrick is the man, answers questions, hard tests, but if you listen in class you'll do fine, anyone who tells you not to take him is just lazy or has trouble paying attention

okay - dr. warrick is a nice guy and he's funny in the goofy science teacher way. He keeps me entertained at 9:20 every MWF - so he must be doing something right. He makes things clear and tries to confirm that we all understand before moving on. Tests - challenging but manageable, the quizzes are only take home. He's really not a bad guy.

He is pretty boring.  His tests aren't that hard, but he often focuses on a limited amount of information from the notes.  Go to class to know what to focus on the tests and just study your notes and you will do fine.

Nice guy...but STUPID as can be. Boring too. At least he writes down all his notes on the whiteboard. But don't expect help outside of class...he doesnt know how to answer questions that deviate from the lab protocol. Tries to stimulate class discussion..but ineffective. Grading got harder as semester proceeded. Quizes are hard. AVOID!

holy crap this guy is boring. definitely knows his stuff, real smart, but that doesn't make it easy. will help if asked, but goes on in class about stuff that has no bearing on what ur learning. goes on tangents too in depth and smart for intro bio.

I had bio teachers in high school that were better than him.  He made me no longer want to major in Bio since he made it the most boring class of all time.  If you're able to, avoid this dude like ebola.
johns the man. if you ask him questions, he'll explain things (eventually), i just get the feeling he's way smarter than everyone else in the room

Dr. Warrick presents the material in a very clear and understandable way. He grades extremely easily, and is a genuinely nice man. However, he is kind of a nervous guy, and his lectures are incredibly boring. He is much better in smaller upper level courses than in Intro to Genetics though.
Great guy, wonderful teacher.  Clear straight forward--really makes you think.
nice guy, but this guy really makes the course suck!
he sucks
Not a fun class. Here's a hint: do not take BIO 201 if your just trying to satisfy your core.

Very nice guy, but sometimes does not explain lab directions clearly.  He tries to make lab fun and help students out if they don't understand concepts so overall he's a pretty good professor for lab.

he's a nice guy and he's really smart. but he'd make a better researcher than a teacher because he explains everything to you like you already know all the stuff he knows. so its really easy to get lost. i would not recommend him for intro to genetics.

Had Dr. Warrick for his first ever semester teaching... he really didn't seem to know how to explain things, and wasn't consistant with grading.  He seems like a very smart man (with his work in neuroscience) but I don't think he should be teaching geneti
He was SUCH a nice nice man and was always willing to help you out. You had to do the work, but if you did you would do well. He knew the subject well and was great!
did not explain the material at all, and always had surprises on tests. not fun at all.
Great teacher.  Helful and besides what other people might say, explains the material very well.  He really knows what he is teaching as well, which helps in genetics
He knows his stuff, would probably be better as a researcher than a professor though.  Nice guy, just not always clear.
Warrick is like the Carson Daly of the bio dept.  He tells you what you need to know, but after the show you sit back and think, "where's the personality?"  Okay, but you gotta show up for class.
